evidence: Cato Agr. 1.2: utī inde exīre possīs
Cic. Att. 12.15.1: nōn exeō inde ante vesperum
terms.comment: The unemphatic “from there”; it answers unde. Also of time, “then, next” (Cic. Fam. 16.9.2).

evidence: Ter. Ad. 4.7.13: illinc hūc trānsferētur virgō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 9.11.3: quī … illinc profectī erant
Plaut. Capt. 603b: Istinc loquere, sī quid vīs

phrases.latin: cumque māne mē in silvam abstrūsī dēnsam et asperam, nōn exeō inde ante vesperum
phrases.english: and once I have hidden myself in the morning in the thick, wild wood, I don’t come out of it before evening

phrases.latin: nōs eō diē cēnātī solvimus; inde austrō lēnissimō caelō serēnō nocte illā et diē posterō in Ītaliam ad Hydrūntem lūdibundī pervēnimus
phrases.english: we set sail that day after dinner; from there, with a very gentle south wind and a clear sky, we reached Italy at Hydrus that night and the next day, as easily as if at play

phrases.latin: inde domum mē ad porrī et ciceris referō laganīque catīnum
phrases.english: from there I take myself home to a dish of leeks and chickpeas and pancakes

phrases.latin: Istinc loquere, sī quid vīs, procul. tamen audiam.
phrases.english: Speak from there, if you want something; I’ll hear you even at a distance.

sources: Lewis & Short: inde · Lewis & Short: illinc · Lewis & Short: istinc
